# Normal Approximation for Poisson Tail Probability

## Setting Up the Problem

For $Y \sim \text{Pois}(n)$:
- $\mathbb{E}[Y] = n$
- $\text{Var}(Y) = n$
- $\sigma_Y = \sqrt{n}$

We want to estimate $P(|Y - n| \geq 2\sqrt{n})$.

## Applying the Normal Approximation (CLT)

A Poisson$(n)$ variable can be decomposed as a sum of $n$ independent $\text{Pois}(1)$ variables. By the CLT, for large $n$:

$$Z = \frac{Y - n}{\sqrt{n}} \;\xrightarrow{d}\; N(0,1)$$

## Computing the Probability

Rewriting the event in terms of the standardized variable:

$$P\!\big(|Y - n| \geq 2\sqrt{n}\big) = P\!\left(\frac{|Y - n|}{\sqrt{n}} \geq 2\right) \approx P(|Z| \geq 2)$$

For a standard normal random variable $Z \sim N(0,1)$:

$$P(|Z| \geq 2) = 2\,P(Z \geq 2) = 2\big[1 - \Phi(2)\big]$$

Using the standard normal CDF value $\Phi(2) \approx 0.97725$:

$$P(|Z| \geq 2) = 2(1 - 0.97725) = 2(0.02275) = 0.04550$$

## Result

$$\boxed{0.0456}$$
